title: Is Human Nature Good?
objective: After this level you can compare Mencius's view that people are born with the sprouts of goodness with Xunzi's view that goodness must be learned.
summary: Mencius held that people are born with four sprouts of goodness to extend; Xunzi held that human nature is bad and goodness is built by artifice and ritual.

cards.headline: A child is about to fall into a well. What do you feel?
cards.body: The Confucian thinker Mencius built a whole theory of human nature on your answer.

cards.headline: The child at the well
cards.body: Mencius, a Confucian of the fourth century BCE, argued that anyone who suddenly saw a child about to fall into a well would feel alarm and compassion. Not to win favor with the parents. Not for praise from the neighbors. Not to escape the sound of crying. The feeling arrives before any calculation, so, he concluded, compassion is part of being human.

cards.headline: Four sprouts
cards.body: Mencius found four such starts in every heart: sympathy, shame, deference to others, and a sense of approving and condemning. They are the sprouts of four virtues: ren (humaneness), rightness, li (ritual propriety) and wisdom. But sprouts aren’t trees. A king who spared an ox from slaughter was urged to extend that same compassion to his suffering people.

cards.headline: Xunzi: goodness is made
cards.body: Xunzi disagreed in a chapter called “Human Nature Is Evil” (his word is closer to “detestable”). We are born fond of profit; follow it, and contention and robbery follow. What is good in us is artifice, wei: habits acquired by conscious effort, through teachers and ritual. His pictures come from crafts. Clay becomes a pot only with a potter, and bent wood is straightened in a press-frame.

cards.headline: Closer than they sound
cards.body: Their quarrel is narrower than it looks. Both held that everyone can become good, with great effort. They split over where the guide lies. Mencius looked inward, to sprouts already in the heart. Xunzi looked outward, to the rituals handed down by the sages, which he thought were the best guide for most people.

cards.headline: Is Human Nature Good?: the big picture
learned: Mencius: the child at the well shows compassion
Four sprouts grow into ren, rightness, li and wisdom
Xunzi: goodness is artifice, like a potter’s pot
Both: anyone can become good, with effort

questions.prompt: What did Mencius call the four feelings, like sympathy and shame, that every heart starts with?

options.label: Rituals
options.rationale: Rituals come from outside, on Xunzi’s view.

options.label: Artifices
options.rationale: Artifice is Xunzi’s word for acquired goodness.

questions.explanation: Mencius called them sprouts: real beginnings of virtue that still have to grow.

questions.prompt: Why did Xunzi insist that people need teachers and ritual to become good?

options.label: Inborn desire for profit, left alone, leads to strife
People are born with fully formed virtues
options.rationale: That’s nearer Mencius, and even he said sprouts must grow.

options.label: Rituals are pleasant for their own sake
options.rationale: His reason is about human nature.

options.label: Teachers were paid by the state

questions.explanation: Born fond of profit, people who simply follow their nature end in contention, so goodness has to be built by conscious effort.

questions.prompt: Mencius’s sprout of deference grows into which virtue that Level 6 met in Confucius?

options.label: Wu wei, acting without forcing
options.rationale: That’s the Daoist ideal of acting without forcing.

options.label: Anatman, non-self
options.rationale: That’s the Buddhist teaching of non-self.

questions.explanation: Deference is the sprout of li, the ritual propriety Confucius prized, done with real feeling.
